quest.title: All Devouring
quest.description: Your training is over and Skirk has located the culprit behind the scenes. Proceed with caution.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x425, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

talks.objective: Go to where the culprit is hiding

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... This is near The Chasm, right?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Yes. If we enter from here, we'll be able to reach that place from your dream.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: You have some experience with Abyssal domains by now, but still, this is someone else's territory. Best to proceed with caution.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry! Paimon's an expert at hiding behind other people for safety!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, but, uh... That means you need to stay safe, {NICKNAME}!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Alright. Remember your training. Time to put it to use.

choices.text: Let's teach this thief a lesson.

talks.objective: Reach the end of the Abyssal corridor

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... Looks like this is a dead end. Did we make it to his hiding place?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, this fog is making it impossible to see anything!

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: #This should be the place where you were attacked, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: The missing part of your soul should be nearby. Can you sense where it is?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (If I close my eyes and focus on the light that came from my wound back then... Yes, I can sense something, and it is nearby. But I can't tell the exact location.)

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Hmm. Our opponent must have covered his tracks just in case. Otherwise, you should have sensed it much more strongly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hold on, look! The spikes are back!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Stay calm. Let's hold back a little, give our enemy some wiggle room so we can see what we're dealing with. If we're too reckless, we might be playing right into his hands.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Our enemy took part of your soul for a reason — it's likely he integrated it into his attacks somehow. If we're smart about this, we can track it down.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ah, {NICKNAME}, Skirk!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What happened? It looked like Skirk just got—

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: In the Guili Plains, you asked me why this enemy chose you as his target.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Now, the answer is clear. It's not just the fact that your strength is impressive. It's also because of your ability to, as you put it, "purify" Abyssal power.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Whatever that actually means... The fact is that ability allowed him to do something that should have been completely impossible:

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Namely, break through my defenses and steal my power.

choices.text: So, you were his real target?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: No, he couldn't have known I'd come to his domain. He only stole your soul fragment because he knew the value of its power. I doubt he expected it to come in handy so soon.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Call it "fate" if you want. I believe that's the term they use in this world for arbitrary coincidences like this.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: In any case, it works to our advantage. Once I realized what he was using that power for, it gave me the chance to get back what you lost.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But, you...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I'll cope.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Well, done gorging? Good. Time to answer some questions.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: How did you get the power of the All-Devouring Narwhal?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The All-Devouring Narwhal!?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohh... of course! Paimon knew that spike thing looked familiar! It looks just like that narwhal's horn!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I highly doubt you acquired that power through your own strength. Tell me I'm wrong.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: You're desperate enough to scour the land for god remains and whatever vestiges of power you can find. That alone proves you wouldn't be able to defeat a creature like that.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Which leaves one possibility — you know my master, "The Foul" Surtalogi.
"The Foul"...
Who dares call him "foul"? Surtalogi...
Surta... logi...!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: What's wrong, bit off more power than you can chew? You're struggling to hold a basic conversation...
Just a little longer. I'm still...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Look! It's back!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Those obsessed with power will let it devour them before abandoning their pursuit.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What should we do now?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Keep calm and use reason to decide the best course of action.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Skirk was stabbed by one of the spikes while retrieving the fragment of my soul, and in the process, some of her power was stolen.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (The culprit is hiding somewhere beyond the fog. I have a good understanding of his attack pattern from the fight just now. If we pursue him, our chances of winning are high.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (But, Skirk's breathing is weaker than usual. If we attack now, I can't guarantee her or Paimon's safety. It's a hard decision to make, but...)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I think we should get out of here.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Wise decision. Final victory doesn't always come after a single battle.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: You've got your soul fragment back, so we both got what we came for. Let the enemy draw breath while he can. It won't be for long.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: #Get us out of here, {NICKNAME}. You'll need to lead the way this time.

choices.text: He was after you from the very beginning?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Phew... Uh... We should be safe here, right?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: I no longer sense his presence. Can't have followed us out of that Abyssal domain.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Weaklings like him will find that my power is not so easily controlled. He won't be leaving that place until he's managed to digest it.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: You seem surprised.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I suppose that's fair... You've seen but a fraction of what that whale is capable of. That gaping maw could swallow a planet whole.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: It's called the All-Devouring Narwhal for a reason — "devouring" is what it does best. It can extract power from anything, dead or alive, as long as it manages to make physical contact.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, when we had our run-in with that thing, Neuvillette mentioned that it has an "instinct to devour"...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Your dragon friend recognized the nature of its abilities and used the power of Hydro to protect you. That worked because it was in a satiated state, so it was somewhat less aggressive than usual.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: It's a different story when it has no more power to feed off of. That's when its true, voracious nature kicks in. It could devour everything on the planet in that state — which is why I cast it into that void space...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: But, I hadn't counted on there being anyone left on this planet capable of wielding its power. To me, that says he must have encountered the whale a long time ago — meaning, he must have known my master.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Yeah, hearing you say "The Foul" definitely got a reaction out of him.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Exactly, it told me everything I needed to know. Hence why I said, we both got what we came for.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: And I believe that brings our transaction to an end. Now that you're whole again, you can get back to your own journey. I'll handle the rest of this situation myself.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No way, we can't leave now! Something was stolen from you because of us! We have to help you get it back!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: This isn't my first taste of failure or losing power. When you fall, you get back up again and become stronger, that's how it is.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But... What if that monster finds you before you're all better?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Plus, how are you gonna get home? It's not like you can just go "swoosh" and open a door to the Abyss again. Not without your full strength!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, sticking with us for the time being doesn't sound so bad, does it?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Fair enough. Then, take this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, what is it?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: A bag of Mora. Nothing in this world is free — I know that much.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I'll leave the planning to you. Hurry up and decide where to go. We shouldn't linger.

choices.text: You said I don't want to be in your debt. Well, I still am.
With its power, he even managed to steal from you of all people...

talks.objective: Go to Bubu Pharmacy to rest and recuperate
Go to Bubu Pharmacy to rest and recuperate

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, this bag from Skirk has a ton of Mora in it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does she have a job or something? Wait, no. After what we saw at Wanmin Restaurant, that seems impossible. Can you imagine? It would go something like...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "I'll be collecting my paycheck now, Boss."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Oh, sure thing! Wait, who are you? Have we met?"

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hm, can't hold a job if you make everyone forget about you. So, what did she do to get all this Mora...?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Ugh... Claimed some buried treasure, took care of a few monsters that were causing trouble... Nothing untoward. It's safe to use.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aaaah! You heard all that?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: A... sonorous voice like yours is hard to miss. I wouldn't be surprised if the sound of it traveled to the nearest mountain top.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then, did you, by chance, happen to hear Paimon's little, um... joke earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: You mean when you called me "Frosty the Lavender Melon"?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No, no. Sorry, Paimon totally misspoke just now. She didn't say that at all! It was... a Paimon look-alike! Yeah, she's a piece of work, that one. Always impersonating Paimon and giving people weird nicknames! Hehe...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #...Okay, fine. The truth is Paimon didn't like you all that much at the start — but things are different now! You helped {NICKNAME} in a big way, so... Whaddaya say? Friends?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I noticed there was only one bed. Go ahead and get some rest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, what about you?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I don't get tired, and I don't need rest. I'm going to practice my sword work. That should help me regain some strength.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But, your shoulder! Hey! Don't just leave!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Argh, whatever. Let her tire herself out. She'll come back eventually.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Let's get some sleep, {NICKNAME}! That comfy bed is calling Paimon!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Skirk is stubborn. Even if I tried to convince her to take it easy, I doubt she'd listen.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Paimon is right. Skirk will stop and take a break once she gets tired... I hope. I should just get some sleep.)
*panting*

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Skirk...?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Of course she's acting like she didn't just get stabbed in the shoulder. Huh, something seems off with her though...)

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: *panting*...

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: ...Quiet.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Who's she talking to? There's no one around. Unless...)

response.speaker: Bewitching Voice
response.text: Do you even remember how many of us perished in that fire? How many bodies were left to rot on the scorched earth? Yet, you alone live on.

response.speaker: Bewitching Voice
response.text: Keep your gaze fixed on your blade. You don't deserve to rest.

response.speaker: Bewitching Voice
response.text: Run, Skirk... Run! Only death awaits us here. Keep running, and don't ever look back...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (Right! In that dream I witnessed, Skirk was training alone, but there were disembodied voices talking to her.)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (One of them mentioned a fire... I wonder what happened exactly. If only she could just talk to us...)

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahhh, getting an early night's sleep is the best! That bed was sooo comfy!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, Skirk? Have you been sitting out here the whole night? The bed's all yours if you want it!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Recovered your strength yet?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: About 60 percent, maybe 70.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, Paimon thought it would take at least a couple of days! That was fast!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: No... Not fast enough.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: That's 20 percent less than last time. Same training regimen, same intensity. Nothing felt different, but somehow, the outcome fell short.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Maybe it's because of the spike that stabbed you?

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: No, I think the problem's with me.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: I need to meditate for the next two days. Deep introspection should help me find the issue.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, sounds intense! We'll watch over you in the meantime, then!

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Thanks. See you in two days.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: From the start, the attacks have been focused on me.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Trying to break through my defenses? I see...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You alright? That thing was...

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: There. I got it back.

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: He'll know something about Master, I'm sure of it... Next time, I need to be ready.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Fine. It was just a scratch.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: It'll take time to recover my strength, of course, but adapting to situations like this is nothing new for me.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Oh, this? It's a "Starcrystal Suit." Abyssal energy is scarce in Teyvat. Wearing this helps me access it more freely.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: It stores concentrated Abyssal energy that I can draw from on the go. When the energy runs out, it reverts back to its original form.

response.speaker: Skirk
response.text: Ah, found somewhere to rest? Well, lead the way then.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: #You look much better, {NICKNAME}. Should I take it that your health issues are resolved?

dialogues.speaker: Changsheng
dialogues.text: Hm, your case was a tricky one. Seems slightly too early to celebrate.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: Very true, Changsheng. Further observation is in order, I think.

dialogues.speaker: Baizhu
dialogues.text: We haven't had many patients recently, so we have several vacant rooms. Feel free to stay a few more days if you need.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Awesome! Thanks!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn*... Time to go? Finally!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Where are we headed?

dialogues.speaker: Skirk
dialogues.text: Just follow me. I'll open an Abyssal rift close to the culprit's location. It will take us to where he's hiding.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We should take Skirk somewhere she can rest! Hmm, but where...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon gets the feeling Skirk wouldn't like being around a lot of people... Oh, wait! Baizhu said we could rest in the back room of the pharmacy, didn't he? Let's head there!
